messages.content: Suppose a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) converge pointwise to f(x) on [0, 1]. Does it follow that the B_n converge uniformly? Ensure that stop words constitute no more than 20% of the total words in your response.

message.content:
No. Pointwise convergence does not imply uniform convergence.

Consider the polynomials \(B_n(x) = (1-x)^n\) on \([0, 1]\). For every fixed \(x \in [0, 1)\), we have \(B_n(x) \to 0\), so \(B_n \to f\) pointwise where \(f(x) = 0\). However,

\[
\sup_{x \in [0,1]} \, |B_n(x) - f(x)| = 1 \quad \text{for every } n,
\]

so the convergence is not uniform. Pointwise convergence is a strictly weaker condition than uniform convergence.
